headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, MCP-enabled travel workspace can ingest ChatGPT Desktop outputs and secrets, creating default-path leakage and cascading action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, while TREK is collaborative and exposes MCP/WebSocket surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where TREK content or ChatGPT outputs can be treated as instructions. The exact parser behavior is undocumented, so I avoid high, but the interaction exists in default-ish workflows.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content is copied into TREK notes or MCP inputs, THEN prompt-like text can steer downstream behavior.
IF TREK exposes collaborative messages through MCP or WebSocket to ChatGPT Desktop, THEN injected instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text between the apps.
Require a human review step before TREK ingests any ChatGPT-generated text.
Restrict MCP endpoints to structured data only.
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels on all cross-app messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, and TREK handles reservations, documents, API keys, and MFA secrets. Because ChatGPT has vendor-only egress and TREK is collaborative with files/logs, sensitive travel data can flow into a third-party inference path without a strong isolation guarantee. This is a default-path leakage risk.
conditions: IF TREK documents, reservations, or secrets are pasted or uploaded into ChatGPT Desktop, THEN those data classes leave the self-hosted boundary.
IF ChatGPT Desktop reads TREK screenshots or app context, THEN sensitive travel data can be transmitted to OpenAI's backend.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets, reservations, or MFA data into ChatGPT Desktop.
Use redacted screenshots only.
Separate TREK production data from any ChatGPT-assisted workspace.
Turn off or limit file uploads for sensitive TREK records.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before cross-app sharing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files and app context, while TREK is real-time collaborative and writes to shared files/logs. Even though ChatGPT cannot write the filesystem, both can act on the same travel artifacts and collaborative state, so conflicting edits or stale overwrites are plausible. The lack of write access on A keeps this below high.
conditions: IF TREK and ChatGPT Desktop edit the same itinerary or document through shared files, THEN stale or conflicting updates can occur.
IF TREK collaborative sessions are active while ChatGPT reads exported copies, THEN divergence between versions can occur.
mitigations: Use one source of truth for itinerary files.
Lock shared documents during ChatGPT-assisted edits.
Export read-only snapshots to ChatGPT.
Review diffs before syncing back to TREK.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency/version checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative travel planner with AI built in, and ChatGPT Desktop can generate plans from files, screenshots, and app context. If TREK treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, reservations, or user-facing travel decisions. Because downstream travel actions can be irreversible, this is high.
conditions: IF TREK imports ChatGPT-generated itineraries without verification, THEN incorrect facts can propagate into reservations or budgets.
IF TREK automates actions from ChatGPT output, THEN a single hallucination can cascade into user-visible travel errors.
mitigations: Require verification before any booking or reservation step.
Show source citations next to imported facts.
Keep ChatGPT output in draft status only.
Add a human approval gate for itinerary changes.
requires-engineering: implement fact-checking against live travel sources.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, and user accounts, while ChatGPT Desktop is vendor-hosted and sends content to api.openai.com. If regulated or sensitive travel data from TREK is routed into ChatGPT, residency and retention obligations can be breached. The pairwise compliance mismatch is therefore material even though exact jurisdictional terms are not fully documented.
conditions: IF TREK stores EU PII, secrets, or reservation records and those are sent to ChatGPT Desktop, THEN residency/retention controls may be violated.
IF an operator uses ChatGPT Desktop on TREK data subject to stricter retention rules, THEN compliance gaps can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ChatGPT prompts.
Classify TREK records before sharing externally.
Use a separate non-regulated test dataset.
Document retention and residency boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for cross-border data flows.
